_comment: The seal codec and cohort verifier. Its own spec because a spec mutates ONE file, and these guards live in seal.rs rather than the ABI surface in lib.rs. The verifier is the one place in this lane where a surviving mutant means a security check that does not check. MOVED 2026-09-16 with `seal.rs` itself, from `kandelo-image-module` into `runtime-core`, so `rootfs::load_image` can authenticate cohorts at the door every caller passes through — the kernel's boot as well as a builder's derived load. The trials are unchanged; only the file they mutate and the crate they verify against moved. The empty-payload pair arrived with the move: `KLZY` has no payload field, so an image described that way reaches the verifier with an empty vector per archive, and refusing it would refuse every pre-`SDEF` image for not saying something its carrier cannot say. Skipping EVERY payload instead disables the check, so both directions are trialled.

trials.name: a cohort short of its expected count still authenticates
the cohort identity is never checked against its seal
members may disagree about their own cohort
one member name may stand for two archives
the cohort identity depends on declaration order
the cohort identity runs its fields together
a payload with trailing bytes decodes anyway
a payload version this reader does not know is guessed at
the cohort digest is not domain-separated
a pending seal is treated as no seal at all
a pending declaration decodes as an absent seal
a cohort already sealed is left as it is instead of recomputed
the producer seals a cohort short of its declared count
the producer lets members disagree about the cohort size
the producer lets two archives share one member name
a pending declaration's count is dropped in the encoding
an EMPTY payload is refused instead of read as no description
any payload is skipped, not only an empty one
